source_refs.note: Exercise 9.2, Question 5 (book p. 272); the book prints no answers for Exercise 9.2; answers checked with sympy and the solution book

blocks.explanation:
Yahan do mukhtalif inverse functions jama ho rahe hain: ek \(\sin^{-1}\) aur ek \(\cos^{-1}\). Jawab \(\sin^{-1}\) mein hai.
Diya kya hai? \(\sin^{-1}\frac{4}{5}\) aur \(\cos^{-1}\frac{12}{13}\).
Find kya karna hai? Jama \(\sin^{-1}\frac{63}{65}\) dikhana hai.
Rule kaunsa? Formula (i), lekin us ke liye dono terms \(\sin^{-1}\) hone chahiye.
Plan: \(\cos^{-1}\frac{12}{13}\) ko triangle se \(\sin^{-1}\) mein badlo, phir formula (i) lagao.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\sin^{-1}\frac{4}{5}\) aur \(\cos^{-1}\frac{12}{13}\).
Maloom karna (prove): in ka jama \(\sin^{-1}\frac{63}{65}\) hai.
Tareeqa: jawab \(\sin^{-1}\) mein hai, is liye formula (i) \(\sin^{-1}x + \sin^{-1}y = \sin^{-1}\left(x\sqrt{1-y^{2}} + y\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\right)\) chahiye. Lekin formula ko dono terms \(\sin^{-1}\) mein chahiye, is liye pehle \(\cos^{-1}\frac{12}{13}\) ko \(\sin^{-1}\) mein badlenge. Yeh bilkul aisa hai jaise rupay aur dollar jama karne se pehle dono ko ek currency mein badalna.

\(\cos^{-1}\frac{12}{13}\) ko \(\sin^{-1}\) mein badlein
\[\beta = \cos^{-1}\tfrac{12}{13},\quad \cos\beta = \tfrac{12}{13}\]
\[\sin\beta = \sqrt{1 - \tfrac{144}{169}} = \tfrac{5}{13}\]
\[\beta = \sin^{-1}\tfrac{5}{13}\]
Kyun: cosine positive hai, is liye \(\beta\) pehle quadrant \(\left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) mein hai. Wahan sine bhi positive hai, aur yeh angle \(\sin^{-1}\) ki principal range mein bhi hai; is liye \(\beta = \sin^{-1}\frac{5}{13}\) likhna jaiz hai. Triangle: adjacent 12, hypotenuse 13, opposite 5.

Formula (i) ki tayyari, \(x = \frac{4}{5},\ y = \frac{5}{13}\)
\[\sqrt{1-x^{2}} = \sqrt{1 - \tfrac{16}{25}} = \tfrac{3}{5}\]
\[\sqrt{1-y^{2}} = \tfrac{12}{13}\]
\[x^{2} + y^{2} = \tfrac{16}{25} + \tfrac{25}{169} \approx 0.79 \le 1\]
Kyun: positive \(x, y\) ke liye formula (i) ki shart \(x^{2} + y^{2} \le 1\) hai, jo poori hai; yani dono angles ka jama \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) se aage nahi jata. \(\sqrt{1-y^{2}}\) dobara nikalne ki zaroorat nahi, yeh wohi \(\frac{12}{13}\) hai jis se shuru kiya tha.

Formula (i) lagayein
\[\text{L.H.S} = \sin^{-1}\tfrac{4}{5} + \sin^{-1}\tfrac{5}{13}\]
\[= \sin^{-1}\left(\tfrac{4}{5}\cdot\tfrac{12}{13} + \tfrac{5}{13}\cdot\tfrac{3}{5}\right)\]
\[= \sin^{-1}\left(\tfrac{48}{65} + \tfrac{15}{65}\right)\]
\[= \sin^{-1}\tfrac{63}{65} = \text{R.H.S}\]
Kyun: \(x\) ko \(y\) ke root se aur \(y\) ko \(x\) ke root se multiply kiya. Denominator \(5 \times 13 = 65\); numerators 48 aur 15; jama 63.
Dhyan dein: badalne wala qadam chhor kar seedha \(\sin^{-1}\frac{12}{13}\) formula mein daal dena bari ghalti hai; \(\cos^{-1}\frac{12}{13}\) aur \(\sin^{-1}\frac{12}{13}\) alag angles hain.

Tasdeeq
\[\sin^{-1}0.8 + \cos^{-1}0.9231 \approx 0.9273 + 0.3948\]
\[= 1.3221\]
\[\sin^{-1}\tfrac{63}{65} \approx 1.3221\ \checkmark\]
Kyun: calculator (radian mode) se dono taraf barabar.
Is check ka faida yeh hai ke agar kahin sign ya number ghalat ho jata to dono taraf ka farq foran nazar aa jata.
